correctness.rationale: The shift-covariant probability p_t=P(X_t=1|X_{s<t}) exists for a stationary binary process. Conditional maximal Bernoulli coupling with independent uniforms makes each Y_t fair even conditional on the complete joint strict past (X,U), hence Y is iid fair and (X,Y) stationary. The mismatch is E|p_t-1/2|. Entropy rate h=E H_b(p_t); concavity plus binary symmetry give h<=H_b(1/2-E|p_t-1/2|), whose increasing inverse gives dbar<=1/2-H_b^-1(h). iid bias p=H_b^-1(h) attains the bound by one-coordinate total variation and coordinatewise joining. Endpoints h=0,ln2 and one-sided natural extensions follow without ergodicity hypotheses.
residual_risks: Reproducible finite checks and existing verification logs never prove unbounded theorems; the above analytic argument supplies the proof.

value.rationale: The complete sharp entropy-versus-Ornstein-distance profile is a canonical quantitative invariant of all binary stationary processes. It improves an unspecified square-root neighborhood to the exact nonlinear boundary at every entropy and supplies saturating processes and an explicit stationary optimal coupling; this is not simply a renamed single-time Pinsker inequality.
residual_risks: Only binary full shift and uniform reference measure; general mixing subshifts/alphabets and classification of all equality laws not proved.

final_claim: For every stationary binary shift process with entropy rate h in [0,ln 2], the sharp Ornstein bar-d upper bound relative to the fair iid binary process is 1/2-H_b^{-1}(h), attained for each h by biased iid Bernoulli processes.
limitations: Only binary full shift and uniform reference measure; general mixing subshifts/alphabets and classification of all equality laws not proved.
